claim: The NVMe admin ioctl NVME_IOCTL_ADMIN_CMD requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN at the kernel level (checked in nvme_user_cmd in drivers/nvme/host/pci.c) — CAP_SYS_RAWIO is insufficient — so containerised or capability-restricted SMART collectors must be granted CAP_SYS_ADMIN to read NVMe health; SATA/SCSI drives need only CAP_SYS_RAWIO.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent running as a non-root, capability-scoped service on NixOS hosts needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN (NVMe) + CAP_SYS_RAWIO (SATA) for SMART telemetry — a NixOS systemd unit AmbientCapabilities design point
scope_conditions: Linux NVMe driver (nvme_user_cmd capability check, verified against v4.4 source by Docker's Justin Cormack and reproduced through 2023); container capability semantics
quoted_support: if you read the source code for NVME_IOCTL_ADMIN_CMD it requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN, so there is nothing you can do except grant that. ... So it looks like --cap-add SYS_ADMIN is required for NVMe drives, but --cap-add SYS_RAWIO is enough for SATA/SCSI drives. If you have a mix of both SATA/NVMe, you must include both flags

claim: smartctl on NVMe without CAP_SYS_ADMIN fails with 'Read NVMe Identify Controller failed: NVME_IOCTL_ADMIN_CMD: Permission denied' (smartctl JSON exit_status 2) — a silent-failure mode the agent must detect and surface rather than reporting as 'no SMART data'.
stance_target: agent SMART collection must distinguish capability failure from absent hardware and report a diagnostic, matching the 'never reliable' complaint in the research query
quoted_support: "Read NVMe Identify Controller failed: NVME_IOCTL_ADMIN_CMD: Permission denied", "severity": "error" ... "exit_status": 2

claim: /run/udev (mounted read-only) is used by the Scrutiny collector for virtual-device filtering and as a fallback to look up WWN device identifiers; without it, serial numbers are used as the device identifier instead.
stance_target: agent device identification should prefer WWN via udev metadata with serial-number fallback — and the agent needs read access to udev data, a NixOS package/permission consideration
scope_conditions: Linux with udev; containerised or host collectors
quoted_support: -v /run/udev is used to retrieve metadata for filtering virtual devices & as a fallback method to lookup WWN device identifiers. Though, if you don't have it, Scrutiny may use your serial number as a device identifier instead.
